Cautiously positive, with added near-term caution from the Beige Book. The FOMC statement highlights solid job gains, moderate growth, and an accommodative, gradual policy stance with transparent balance sheet normalization. Incorporating the August 2017 Beige Book nudges the outlook softer at the margin: Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, and Maria disrupted energy and natural gas production (notably Eagle Ford) and logistics along the Gulf Coast, with impacts noted in the Dallas and Atlanta Districts; agricultural conditions were mixed. These storm-related effects introduce short-term downside risks and supply bottlenecks but are expected to be temporary. Combined with the July 2017 SLOOS showing softer loan demand and some tighter standards in CRE and consumer credit (partly offset by easier residential mortgage standards), credit appetite/availability looks mixed-to-soft outside housing. Financial stability considerations remain balanced: elevated valuations and pockets of leverage versus strong bank capital/liquidity. Net result: the growth/labor backdrop remains mildly positive, but Beige Book storm disruptions and SLOOS softness warrant a slightly more cautious, data-dependent stance.
